## What is reproducibility?

\

In scientific research, a result is:

:::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}

- *reproducible* if performing the same analysis on the same dataset produces the 
  same result
- *replicable* if performing the same analysis on a different dataset produces 
  qualitatively similar answers
:::
:::{.column width="50%}

- *robust* if performing a different analysis (that tries to answer the same 
  question) on the same dataset produces similar or identical answers
- *generalisable* if we can run different analysis workflows on different 
  datasets and get similar answers

:::
:::

![](/img/reproducibility_matrix.jpg){width=50%, fig-align="center"}

## Why is reproducibility important?

\

In the context of scientific computing/analysis, we want to be able to:

- Verify our own results
- Verify the results of others

By making our work reproducible, we ensure that both these things are not just
possible, but straightforward!

## Reproducibility in Earth sciences

Other findings:

- 82% of researchers are self taught programmers
- 40% do not know who legally owns the code they are writing
- More than 35% of respondents say it can take 2-3 weeks to train a new PhD with the
  research software used by the group
  - 23% said up to one year, 8% said more than a year!

::: footer
[R Reinecke et al (2022)](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1748-9326/ac5cf8)
:::

## Additional benefits

- Reproducibility is not just for scientific results
- By making our software more reproducible, we also get to reap the benefits!

:::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
### Safely implement changes

- Automation and testing help catch mistakes before they become an issue
:::
:::{.column width=50%}
### Rerun analyses

- Better documentation to get started
- Create reusable pipelines to need for manually running commands
- Untangle data from code so analysis can run on different inputs
:::
:::

:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
### Simpler for new team members to get started

- Better documentation on how to use the software
- Relevant metadata present - no hunting down dependencies
:::
:::{.column width=50%}
### Better collaboration

- Version control
- Accessibility of code and data
:::
:::

## Where do we go from here...


Throughout the rest of this session, we will walk through the steps that we can
take to go from an ad hoc collection of scripts into a reproducible scientific 
workflow!

Reproducibility must haves:

- Version Control
- READMEs
- Licenses
- Automation
- Testing
